symptom: `mxcli layout flows` introduced MPR008 overlaps at merge nodes on the main path (ako/mxcli#684, after the reporter's correction 2, not 4): '(merge)' (2355,80) and '(merge)' (2360,80) 5px; '(merge)' (2815,1730) and '(unnamed)' (2740,1730) 75px.
cause: Not a layout-flows defect: layout flows rebuilds with the CREATE builder, and the builder places an IF's closing merge from the measured width of its branch. A decision inside the branch was measured from its split's centre and from the branch's left edge although it starts 15px in (ako/mxcli#1773), so the closing merge landed in the activity — or the inner merge — before it.
insight: Grade the layouter with the linter, as the reporter proposed, but do it where the positions are computed: assertNoSharedPlace (MPR008's box test with stored sizes) plus loopEscapes (MPR011) over a handful of shapes in five contexts (main line, loop body, THEN, ELSE, THEN-without-ELSE) reproduced the merge-into-activity overlap in 11 shape/context pairs with no project; the reporter's project was not needed. Reconstruct shapes by mechanism (what places a merge: a measured branch width), not by guessing the reporter's flows. The real-tool control on a fresh 11.14.0 app: flows exec'd by the pre-fix binary lint 5 MPR008; after `layout flows` with the fix, 3, all pre-existing and of other classes (a CASE's multi-value merge on its first activity; two vertical collisions from heights that are not symmetric about the line), dry-run then idempotent, mx check 0 errors. The note that lost `position:` after layout is not lost: layout flows re-places notes by design and describe omits a note's position when it is the default one above its activity.
